nodes.name: ZIF-8 Crystallization with Metal Precursors
nodes.procedure: During the crystallization of ZIF-8 (average size d = 50 nm), ruthenium acetylacetonate (Ru(acac)3) and chromium nitrate nonahydrate (Cr(NO3)3·9H2O) were added, and silica (SiO2) was used as a template to increase the surface area of the formed ZIF-8.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis, Etching, and Calcination
nodes.procedure: The sample was pyrolyzed at 950°C in an Ar atmosphere to evaporate Zn, followed by the removal of SiO2 in a NaOH solution. After the second calcination, the catalysts were obtained. The catalysts contain only Ru NPs (RuNPs-N-C), a mixture of Ru NPs and SAs (RuNPs-RuSAs-N-C) and only Cr SAs (CrSAs-N-C) were also prepared following the same procedure.

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD patterns exhibit characteristic broad peaks at ≈25° and 43° corresponding to (002) and (101) planes of graphitic carbon with no peaks for Ru and Cr metal nanoparticles.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The powder XRD patterns of the Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C, Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C, and Cr_{SAs}-N-C samples (Figure S4, Supporting Information) exhibit characteristic broad peaks at ≈25 and 43° corresponding to the (002) and (101) planes of graphitic carbon, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru loading of 1.28 wt.% and Cr loading of 0.08 wt.% in Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C; Ru content of 1.15 wt.% in Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The loading of Ru and Cr is found to be 1.28 and 0.08 wt.% for Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C respectively by inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) analysis.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectra show D and G bands at ≈1350 and 1590 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G ratio of 1.2 for Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C and 1.01 for Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The intensity ratio of D to G (I_D/I_G) is calculated to be 1.2 and 1.01 for Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C and Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals rhombic dodecahedron morphology with particle size ≈500 nm; Ru NPs uniformly dispersed with average size 1.5-2.5 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The TEM images (Figure S8a,b, Supporting Information) reveal a uniform dispersion of Ru_{NPs} on the support, with an average particle size ranging from 1.5 to 2.5 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM reveals co-existence of nanoparticles and single atoms; Ru-Cr diatomic structure (RuCr_{APs}) with average interatomic distance ≈3.0 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The second forms a Ru-Cr diatomic structure (RuCr_{APs}) with an average interatomic distance of ≈3.0 Å (Figure 1g and h, linear scan profile of region 1 and 2 in Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping confirms presence of C, N, Ru, and Cr; Ru exists as mixture of NPs and SAs, Cr as single atoms with no aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS) mapping (Figure 1c-e and Figure S8d, Supporting Information) confirms the presence of C, N, Ru and Cr.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows slightly higher edge position than Ru foil indicating average Ru valence >0; FT EXAFS confirms Ru-Ru coordination number 2.3±0.6 at 2.69 Å and Ru-N bonds; Cr K-edge FT EXAFS shows Cr-N at 1.95 Å and Ru-Cr at 2.54 Å confirming RuCr atomic pairs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XANES data at the Ru K-edge (Figure 2a) reveal the K-edge position of Ru in both Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C and Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C is slightly higher compared to that of Ru foil, suggesting that the average valence state of Ru in these structures is greater than zero.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p spectra of Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C shift to lower binding energy compared to Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C, indicating lowered oxidation states due to RuCr atomic pairs.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XPS analysis shows that Ru 3p spectra of Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C (Figure S11b, Supporting Information) shift to lower binding energy compared to Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS fitting shows charge transfer resistance R_CT (R_3) of 38.83 Ω for Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C compared to 73.41 Ω for Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C exhibits ... the fastest charge transfer kinetics with R_3 value of 38.83Ω (Figure S12 inset, Table S1, Supporting Information) compared to that of Ru_{NPs}-Ru_{SAs}-N-C (73.41Ω).

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical surface area (ECSA) of Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C calculated as 205.07 m²·g⁻¹ based on copper underpotential deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ECSA of Ru_{NPs}-RuCr_{APs}-N-C is calculated to be 205.07 m²·g⁻¹, implying its abundant active sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Crystal plane distance measured as 0.23 nm corresponding to (10-10) plane of hexagonal Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The distance between the crystal planes of the metal particles is measured to be 0.23 nm, corresponding to the (10-10) plane of hexagonal Ru (Figure S8e, Supporting Information).
